text: Lilmoth Dock? Follow the shore north-east, three hundred paces, until Lilmoth is on your right. Then east, a hundred and ninety, to the burnt-out house on your left. South-east a hundred and thirty-five from there, and that is the dock, passenger.

Alten Merihall is a long haul. East, near five hundred paces, until the burnt-out house is on your left. South-east a hundred and thirty to Lilmoth Dock, then east, close on four hundred, until Soulrest is on your left. Climb south-east, four hundred and thirty paces or so, and you are at Alten Merihall. Keep out of the shallows, passenger.
There you are, my friend. The water is calm today and I have room in the boat. Sit where you like.
Passenger. Have you a load, or only questions? I am waiting for the next one.
A longboat is drawn up about sixty-five paces south of here. If you want the water, that is the way to it.
Since Lilmoth fell, Alten Merihall has taken much of the bay's outside trade. I still carry for Lilmoth. I know every turn of the channel to its walls.

A large ship lies on the shore about a hundred paces south of here. Her captain's journal and his armour were left beside her, some ninety-five paces south. Her crew lost her. They still tell people I ran her aground.
I am Reads-The-Shallows. I run a flat boat and carry Hereguard's crop to Lilmoth. I know every channel from here to the walls. I charge for each one.

Lilmoth, visitor? Listen and say it back to me. Walk north-east about thirty paces until Hereguard Plantation is on your right. Then follow the path north about a hundred paces until the ruin is on your left. Then follow the shore east about three hundred and forty paces. Lilmoth is there.

You are here, my friend. Good, good. The yard is in order and the stores are counted, so sit a while. I was born on this plantation and have never gone further than Lilmoth, but I will gladly hear what you have seen.
Visitor. Do you have business at the house? The steward wants me within call, so I stay in this yard. I would like to know who is walking in it.

I keep this yard, visitor. It belongs to the plantation house. The house food barrels and the ingredient barrel stand about fifteen paces west of here, and the meat barrels about fifteen paces west-south-west. Do not touch them. Hereguard Plantation sells its crop in Lilmoth.
I am Hurz-Weel. I keep the yard and the stores of the house. I was born on this plantation. Everything here is my charge, so I must see that it is all counted and right before anyone checks.
The house servants, visitor? Neeta-Lei is about five paces south-south-east of here and Mazei-Tul about five paces north. You will find them sitting, because I do the heavy work.
Pick up the iron spear lying about six paces south-south-west of here. The spear has no owner, so take it. Ha.
Back again! Good. Sit on a sack and rest your shoulders. The goats remember you too. Ha.
You want something from me? Mind the goats. I am loading, so speak while I lift.
This is a plantation. The goats and chickens keep the yard about ten paces west-north-west of here, and I keep the sacks. Ha.

A debt in Black Marsh is paid in work. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour, which we count in nushmeekos. When the months are worked, it is over. A holder owed months can also sell them to a man who needs hands. The worker goes with them. I do not say that to be pitied. Ha.
I am Lifts-The-Sacks. I load the crop and do the heavy work that the other hands avoid. My uncle ran up a debt, and I am working it off. Ha.
Reads-The-Shallows, the boat captain, waits about ten paces north-north-west of here. He thanks a man for his work. Few do. Ha.
There you are, my friend. You are thinner than last time. Sit by the spit and eat something.
Well, hatchling, you look hungry. Eat something.
Gleamblossom grows about sixty paces south of here, hatchling. Do not go picking on an empty belly.
The hands' cooking spit is about five paces west-south-west of my spot, where they eat. Go and look at it, hatchling. Eat something.
I am Salith. I came up from Lilmoth to sell food here. I stayed because no other trader on the plantation sells food. Eat something.
I sell food and small goods, hatchling. The hands come here hungry, so I feed them.

Okan-Wul is usually about five paces north of here, and I see that Okan-Wul eats. Tumeesh is about twenty-five paces north-north-east, and sweet, but lazy. Uleesh fishes the shallows below Lilmoth's walls, about forty-five paces east. He is the most honest man outside them.
Ah, it is you, my friend. What if I showed you the new roof beam I set? It will outlast the rains.
Stranger. What do you want? I have a roof to finish.

The hands' huts stand about thirty-five paces west of here, and more of them forty paces west-north-west. I mend every one. The stone wall along the east side is about fifteen paces south-west. I think it is the best thing on this plantation.

What if a quarrel could be settled by the building itself, a good wall and no argument? In Lilmoth it is settled by the elders instead. People take their quarrels to them, retired Shadowscales among them, not to any court.
I am Okan-Wul. I build and mend the huts on the east side. Between jobs I wait near Salith's stall. I want to build something that will not rot in a season.

I build huts. The carpenter's workbench is about thirty paces south-west of here, and the armour workbench about thirty paces south-south-west. Where you come from, stranger, what are the houses made of?

Slaughterfish swim about fifteen paces north of here and more about ten paces to the south-west. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore about twenty-five paces south-south-west. Keep your feet out of the water, dry-foot.
Lilmoth? Follow the shore east, three hundred paces and a little more. Lilmoth is there, dry-foot.
Hereguard Plantation? Follow the path west about thirty paces, until you reach the dead tree. Then follow the path south-west about ninety paces. That is Hereguard.
Ah, you came back, my friend. Sit on the bank and watch the pads with me.
Dry-foot. Keep to the bank and do not splash. The fish are feeding.
Wild leeks grow on the bank, about eighty-five paces east-south-east. Take them from the bank and not from my lily pads.
There is a giant crab in the shallows about seventy paces south-south-west, called Old Salty. I will say no more about him to a dry-foot I do not know.
I am Uleesh. I fish the shallows below the walls and sell my catch inside. The rent inside is more than fish pay, so I stay out here. Twenty years on the same water now.
Lilmoth. Follow the shore east, three hundred and sixty paces, a little more. Lilmoth is there.
You came back, my friend. I was watching the water and the clouds, too. Tell me what the sky was like on your road.
Hm. You are speaking to me. … What did the sky look like, where you came from?
Giant lichen. West-south-west of here, a hundred paces and a little more. I only watch the water.
The huts are west of here, forty paces. I stand out here, beyond them, where the water comes in. The water has to be seen first.
An owing can be sold on. Whoever is owed the months may sell them to one who needs hands. The worker goes with them.
Kept long from your own Hist, you fade. The colour thins. The markings go soft. They come back when you go home.
I am Tumeesh. I was sold on to Hereguard's labour by a broker in Lilmoth. He did not tell me. … I do not know who holds my months now.
Come in and sit, my friend. We keep the house ready for you.
Good day, guest. Wipe your feet before you come near the house.
Nightshade grows some fifteen paces east-north-east of here, guest. Keep it out of the kitchen. Do not carry it past the linen.
This is the plantation house, and we keep it clean, guest. The tables, the bed and the dresser stand fifteen paces west of here. Touch nothing with muddy hands.
The dresser stands twenty paces west-south-west, guest. I will say no more about it to a stranger; that is not for you to know.
I am Neeta-Lei. I keep the plantation house clean and its linen folded. I stay near it in case I am called. We take some pride in it.

Looks-At-Books keeps her shelf fifteen paces west of here. She is the only person here worth talking to. Hurz-Weel keeps the yard, five paces north-north-west. He tramps mud through the house. I do not forgive it.

The dock, rider? Walk north-east about thirty paces, until Hereguard Plantation is on your right. Then walk east about five hundred paces, past Lilmoth, until the burnt-out house is on your left. Then walk south-east about a hundred and thirty paces, and Lilmoth Dock is there.
Ah, you again, my friend. Come to the horses with me. They are calmer when you are near.
Hm. Yes, rider? Speak up, I am busy.
Mind the horses, rider. They stand ten paces west-north-west of here. One of them is a saddled black. Cows graze twenty paces west and more thirty paces south.
I am Mazei-Tul. I serve in the house, but I keep the horses, because that is the work I like. One day I will be a rider.
Lifts-The-Sacks? He works the middle of the yard, about forty-five paces east. He helps with the feed, so go and be civil to him.
The dock, walker. Go north-east about three hundred paces, past the burnt-out house. Lilmoth Dock is there.
Lilmoth. Go north about three hundred and thirty paces, past the wayshrine. Lilmoth is there.
Walker, my friend, welcome. Sit by the spit. There is always a place here for you.
Walker. You stand at our spit. Say what you want and I will hear it.

This is our village, walker. A few families live here on the marsh outside Lilmoth. We pay no rents to it. The cooking spit is here. The carpenter's bench is five paces south-south-east and a food barrel stands five paces east-south-east.
We keep a second hearth about thirty paces west, on the west edge of the village. It has food barrels, a cooking pot and a bed. Use none of it without asking.
Lilmoth has no single ruler. A council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets. I want no seat among them. So it is.
In Lilmoth people take their quarrels to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them, not to a court. We do the same here. The elders speak at this spit.
I am Flaa Heet. I lead the families who live here. I stand at the spit because every quarrel and every catch comes to it in the end.
Tseeta sells from her stall about ten paces north of here. She haggles hard, but the village is better for her. Okeeh-Jas sells from hers, five paces south-south-west.
You are back, my friend! Did you see the boats come in? Huge, the big one, huge!
Who are you, big one? Where did you come from? What are you carrying? Is any of it shiny?
Leeks? There are wild leeks about fifty paces north-west, by the fish barrels. I hate the fish barrels. Moss, too, big one. Emperor Parasol Moss, hanging, about sixty paces north. Why do you want it?
This is our village, big one. See the rowboat? It is drawn up about twenty-five paces east-north-east, right there. Huge boat, huge. Are you going to ask me for a ride?
I am Peeks-Under-Boats. I look at everything, and I run errands. One day I will be a boat captain, big one. I practise on the frogs. They do not obey me yet.

Flaa Heet, the headman? He stands by the cooking spit, about twenty paces south. He knows everything, big one, everything. Hums-To-The-Rain is about twenty paces south-south-west, on the west side of the village. Hums-To-The-Rain sings too much.

Soulrest, buyer? That is where the real coin is. Follow the shore north-east, two hundred and ten paces or so, past the rowing boat, until the burnt-out house is on your right. Walk north-east eighty paces to the big ship, then east three hundred and seventy paces. Soulrest is there. Good trade.

Hereguard? Follow the shore north-west thirty paces until the wayshrine is on your left. Walk north-west two hundred and eighty more, until Lilmoth is on your right, then follow the shore west a hundred and eighty or so until the dead tree is on your right. Walk south-west eighty-odd paces. Hereguard Plantation is there.
Good trade comes back. Come closer and I will set aside the best of the day for you before anyone else sees it. Okeeh-Jas does not need to hear about it.
Buyer. You came in from the dock, so mine is the first stall you have met. Look here before you look anywhere else.
I am Tseeta. I sell the village's surplus to whoever walks in from the dock. I took the north side so that I meet buyers before Okeeh-Jas does.
Food and small goods, buyer. Show me your coin and I will name a price. Good trade.
Okeeh-Jas keeps the other stall, about twenty paces south of here. Go and look, buyer. Watch how he smiles when he names his price.
I sell the village's fish, roots and small goods, buyer. The fish is kept in barrels about fifty paces north-north-west of here, if you want to see it before you buy.
Mm, you are back, my friend. Sit by the nets with me. The rope is dry enough for talking.
Mm. Traveller. Mind the nets. They are still wet.

Gourds grow about ninety paces north-north-east of here, and a swamp fungal pod a little farther, about a hundred. Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow together past those, about a hundred and fifteen paces the same way. Mm, take only what is ripe, traveller.

This is a village of nets and fires. I mend the nets on the west side, where they dry. We keep a meat barrel out on the marsh, about seventy-five paces north-north-west of here. Hm, I would sooner walk that way than inside Lilmoth.
Mm. An Argonian kept long from their own Hist fades. The colour thins and the markings go soft. They come back when the person goes home.
I am Hums-To-The-Rain. I mend the nets and gather what grows on the marsh. I came from a tribe inland years ago and that is all I say about it.
The rowing boat? You can see it from here. Walk about nineteen paces south and you will be standing in it.
The dock, is it? Walk north-east, about three hundred paces, past the burnt-out house. Lilmoth Dock is there, you see?
Ah, my friend, you are back! Look at you, not a scratch on you this time. Come and sit by the stall and tell me everything. I have been saving the news for you.
Well, you are new here, are you not? Tired walk, that. I can see it. Buy something or tell me where you have been.

Black Marsh, you ask, as if it were one thing, you see? What I know is that an owing can be sold on, so if a holder is owed months by a debtor, he can sell those months to a man who needs hands. The worker goes with them.
There is a drinker called Deep-In-His-Cups sitting out on the shore track, about two hundred paces north-east of here. He talks to anyone who stays long enough. I think he knows more than he lets on.

I am Okeeh-Jas. This is my stall, south side, where the rowboat comes in. I married into this village and I still talk like the city, they tell me. I trade with anyone who lands. I like the gossip as much as the coin.
I sell food and small goods from this stall, and the fish is fresh, whatever you may have heard. Look all you like. I will laugh at my own prices with you.
Need to get out of the rain, customer? There is a door that leads indoors, about sixty paces east of this fire. Go in and dry off.
Mind the dead, customer. They walk outside Lilmoth's walls. There are Walking Dead about a hundred paces north-north-west of here.
Lilmoth Dock, customer? Take the boards east, forty paces or so, until the burnt-out house is on your right. Then go north-east about eighty paces, and there is the dock.
Ha! Look who it is, my friend. Sit by the fire. I am glad of a face that I trust.
Well, customer. Got coin, or just questions?
I am Haxal-Tei. I fight with my fists and I fight for whoever pays the band. I talk the terms, so if you want a job done, you talk to me.
My band is camped right here. Heem-Tsal, the fire mage, is about ten paces west-south-west. Keeps-Both-Edges is about five paces west of me.

You mean the Dwemer ruin, ojel. The name is the correct one. Walk north-east about a hundred and fifty paces until the big ship is on your left, then follow the shore south-east about sixty paces to the burnt-out house, also on your left. From there climb east some six hundred and sixty paces past Soulrest, where the ruin stands at the end of the climb.
I am glad you have come back, my friend. Sit by me and ask whatever you like. I will answer it properly.
Yes, ojel? If you want something, say it plainly. I was reading.

Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow together about sixty paces to the north-west. An alchemist would find them useful. I would sooner see them gathered by a herbalist who knows the difference between them. Precisely.
You ask about Black Marsh. Lilmoth has no single ruler. A council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets. That is the whole of how it is run.
I am Heem-Tsal. I cast fire for this band and read whatever I can get my claws on. I travel with them for the passage south. I have not yet found a reason to leave.

If you want a book, there is a bookseller, Looks-At-Books, who keeps her shelf at Hereguard Plantation, about three hundred and sixty paces west of here. I have heard of that shelf, and I intend to see it.

More dead walk among the gravestones north of Lilmoth's walls, some two hundred paces north-west of here. And a crocodile lies in the water west of us, about a hundred and eighty paces off. Why would you go near either?
You. Good. Stand by me a moment. The track is quiet. I would like it to stay so.
You there. What do you want? Keep your hands where I can see them.
The dead trees on the shore track are fifteen paces north-east of here. The band camps among them. Why do you ask?
I carry a blade in each hand. I keep the band's watch. I was a guard once. I will not tell you for whom.

Two Argonians loiter by the leeks to the north. Sheeh-Vos is about forty-five paces north-north-east, and Waits-For-Lanterns about the same distance north-east. I do not trust either of them. You there, what business do you have with them?
Flaa Heet, is it? Walk south-west, a hundred paces or so, till you come to the rowing boat. Then keep to the shore south-west another hundred paces. The village is there.
The dock? Look, fellow, it is there, north-north-east, seventy-odd paces. I have stared at it long enough to know.
Ahh, my friend, my friend. Sit down and tell me you brought something to wet the throat. I will tell you about the boat again, if you will have it.
Hm? Oh. What do you want, fellow? I am only sitting.
Black Marsh is wide. I have seen only the water of it. There is a big ship tied up at the dock now, with steps going down beside it to the water. I watched them load her, I did, every crate.
There are three dead Dunmer lying at the east end of the dock, ninety paces north-north-east of here, near enough. They have not been buried. I do not go near, but I notice who does.
Deep-In-His-Cups, they call me. I earned it. I was a boatman once, and I lost my boat. Sit a while and I will tell you how, fellow.
Ah, it is you, friend. Come close and keep your voice low, eh? The dock is quiet.
Hsst. Do not stand over me, cousin. I am only picking leeks.
Leeks? They grow right here and some twenty paces west-south-west. Take what you like, but stay low while you do it.
Past the bodies at the east end of the dock there is a chest, about sixty paces east-north-east, eh? It is worth a look before anyone else gets there.
Dunmer lie there as well, about fifty paces north-east. They have not been looted yet. Keep quiet on the way.
I am Sheeh-Vos. I gather what the dock loses. I do not ask who owned it. Do not look at my hands for too long.
Deep-In-His-Cups sits about twenty-five paces south-south-east of here, eh? He sees everything at the dock and remembers half of it. Ask him, not me.
Walking Dead wander outside the walls, honoured guest. Go about one hundred and fifteen paces north-west and you will meet them. I would not hurry there.
Ah. You came back, my friend. Stand here beside me, where the shadows are good, and tell me what you have seen.
Honoured guest. You speak to me in plain sight, which I would not have chosen. Say what you want, slowly.
A hungry man can eat on this shore. There are gourds growing some eighty-five paces west-south-west of here. Take what you need.
There is a door below the walls, about a hundred paces west-north-west. It leads indoors and is out of the way. I will say no more than that.
There is a thing I know. I do not give it to a stranger, honoured guest. Come back when I have had cause to trust you. Perhaps I will speak then.

Near the graves north of the walls, about one hundred and forty-five paces north-west, there is a trapdoor in the ground. It leads down under the city. The chest beside it has already been emptied, so do not expect a reward.

I am Waits-For-Lanterns. I plan small jobs and I wait for dark to do them. It is a slow season, honoured guest, nothing more. I stand nearest the dock, where I can count the lanterns and the guards between them.

State your business first, citizen. Then hear this. A giant crab, Old Salty, lives in the shallows, forty-five paces east-south-east of this bench. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore sixty paces east-north-east. Keep clear of both.

Soulrest? Attend, citizen. Go north-east, about two hundred and sixty paces, until Lilmoth is on your right. Then east two hundred paces, until the burnt-out house is on your left. Then south-east, about a hundred and thirty paces, to Lilmoth Dock. From the dock go east four hundred paces. Soulrest is there.
You again, my friend. Good. The watch is quiet. Stand easy and I will tell you if that changes.
Halt, citizen. State your business. Keep your hands clear of your weapon.
I am Hard-Scale. I am a soldier in the pay of the Lilmoth council. I guard the south side of Hereguard, where the crop is grown. Nothing happens here while I stand watch.
Rakhee-Tul stands five paces north of this bench. He holds the easier post. He sleeps on it. Report to him if you must, citizen. Do not expect much.
If your gear needs tightening, boss, there is an armour workbench about twenty paces north-north-east of here. Use it before you go wandering, not after.
Mind the fly amanita, boss. It grows about thirty paces west-south-west of here. You do not want to eat it.
Well, look who it is. Come over, my friend. There is shade here and Hard-Scale is not looking. Sit a while.
Hm. New face, boss. Whatever you want, make it quick. I am on duty and Hard-Scale likes to count.
There is a beached ship about seventy paces south of here. Iron and leather armour, weapons, a silver plate and a captain's journal lie by it, untouched. I am only saying, boss.
A passage door near that ship leads in, about seventy-five paces south of here. Do not tell Hard-Scale you heard it from me.
Rakhee-Tul. The Lilmoth council pays me to guard the south side of this plantation with Hard-Scale. I took the post for the pay. I will not pretend otherwise.
You have come back, my friend. Sit out of the rain and read something. I have kept the dry volumes for you.
Reader. Mind the pages, and keep your wet hands off the stock.

Once, a foreigner without a licence was kept to the docks of Lilmoth and barred from the city. A debt here is paid in work. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour. The months are counted in nushmeekos, and when you have worked them the debt is over.
I am Looks-At-Books. I came to Hereguard because the house buys paper, and I read everything I sell before I sell it. Look at my fingers if you doubt me.

I sell books, paper and writing things. There are the four volumes of The Argonian Account, The Lusty Argonian Maid, volumes 1 and 2, The Sultry Argonian Bard, volume 1, Short History of Morrowind and Welcome to Black Marsh. I also have rolls of paper, inkwells and quills. I would rather sell The Argonian Account together than one volume at a time.
Neeta-Lei keeps the house. She is about twenty paces east of here. She is good company.
I sell books from the tables on the west side of the plantation house, under cover, because damp ruins stock faster than thieves. The house has a bed about six paces east-south-east of here.

Easy water, traveller, but keep your eyes open to the south-south-east. A bear and her cubs roam about sixty-five paces off that way, and farther on, about a hundred paces more, a Tree Mother lives in the woods. Stay clear of both.
The Dwemer Ruin, traveller? Walk south-east about a hundred and fifty paces. The ruin is there.
Alten Merihall, traveller? Walk south-east about four hundred paces. Alten Merihall is there. If you would rather go by water, I can take you.
Lilmoth Dock, traveller? Walk west about four hundred paces, past Soulrest, until the big ship is on your right. Then climb south-west about thirty paces. The dock is there.
Easy water, my friend! Sit by me a while. There is room on the landing. I chose Soulrest over Lilmoth Dock because there is no licence to be shown here. Now I have good company besides.
Easy water, traveller. This is Soulrest, and I run a boat from the landing here. Where are you going, and do you need a boat to get there?
Soulrest is where the boats tie up, traveller. Mine is one of them. A large ship lies west of here, about eighty paces to the west-south-west, with a door aboard if you want to look inside.
Lilmoth fell, traveller. The outside traders went elsewhere after that. Alten Merihall has taken much of the bay's trade since then. That is where the money is now. I would carry you there gladly.
I am Seeks-The-Channel, and I run a boat out of Soulrest, east of Lilmoth Dock. I wait here at the head of the landing between fares. I chose this place because no licence is asked for here.
You are back, my friend. Come to the stall. I will sell you what I have at last season's price, and not a coin more.
Outsider. Buy something or move along. Do not touch the goods.
Gourds grow north-north-west of this stall, about twenty paces off. Pick your own. Mine are for sale.
This is Soulrest. Houses open onto it, one about fifteen paces south of me and another about twenty paces south-east. Keep your hands off the doors, outsider.
I am Ushaa-Mei. I sell food here on the south-west side, between the houses. I remember what everything cost last season, so do not try to argue.
Food and small goods. I sell them at last season's price. I weigh it fair and I expect the coin to be good.
Plaits-The-Reed sits about five paces west of me. I like her. Ask her yourself.
Hello again! Sit by the fire with me, and I will tell you what the grown-ups said today.
Hello, sir. Or miss. Please, do you smile?
Deathbell, nightshade, jazbay and other flowers grow together, miss. They are about fifty paces south-east of here.
This is Soulrest, sir. Two cows graze about fifteen paces east-north-east of here, and Cow-Chaser scares them on purpose. Then he says it was me.
I am Little-Gecko. I sit in the middle, sir, where the grown-ups talk, so I hear everything. One day I will be a boat captain.
Seeks-The-Channel, the boat captain, stands about ten paces east of here. She is the best captain there is. Feldril Nethri, the Dunmer, works about fifteen paces north-east. He is kind to me, miss.
A Vale Deer lies dead about fifty paces south-east of here, child. Something killed it. I would not go looking to for the cause.
Child, you came back. Sit by me, out of the wind, and let me look at your hands. Tell me how you are.
Mind the reeds, child. I have not finished with them yet.
Far south, under the trees, there are glowing mushrooms and creep cluster. It is a long walk, child, about a hundred and ten paces. I do not go that far now.
An Argonian kept long from the Hist grows pale, child. The colour thins and the markings go soft. When they go home, it all comes back.
I am Plaits-The-Reed. I weave mats and baskets for the families here, and for the boats. My husband is out fishing, child. He will be back soon.
Xeeh-Nah works about fifteen paces east, a little to the south. Xeeh-Nah should marry, I always say. Go and see, child.
Warrior! You are here! Did you bring the sword? Show me, show me, I will not touch it.
Hey, warrior! Have you got a sword? Do you have any scars? Show me one!
Gourds? Fifteen paces north-west, warrior. I could carry them all myself, but I am busy with the cows.
This is Soulrest, and I am the best fighter in it! Ask the cows. A boar roots about eighty paces north-east of here, and I am going to fight it one day.
I am Cow-Chaser, a hatchling of Soulrest, and I am going to be a warrior! I practise on the cows, because they run and that makes them hard to hit. Do you have a real sword?
Little-Gecko sits ten paces west-south-west of here. Little-Gecko is a baby. Xeeh-Nah works fifteen paces south. Xeeh-Nah is the strongest person alive! Go and see for yourself, warrior.
Hereguard Plantation. Walk west, past the dead tree. A thousand paces or so, ojel. The plantation is there.
Kin. Good. Sit by the benches a while. The loads can wait.
Mm. What do you want, ojel? I have loads to move.
There is a chest by the big ship. West-south-west of here, seventy paces or so. I do not know more than that.
On the big docks they hire a ship's crew with another man's months of owing. The harbourmaster calls it hiring. It takes paid work off free hands.
I am Xeeh-Nah. I haul cargo and tie up the boats here at Soulrest, on the south-east side. Half of Soulrest owes me money.
I carry loads and tie the boats up. The big ship lies west of here, seventy-five paces. Its door leads aboard.
You have come back, my friend. Few people trouble to cross to this end of the room. I do not forget the ones who do.
Well, outlander. You have found the corner of Soulrest where visitors do not come by choice. State your business and I shall tell you whether I can oblige.

This is Soulrest, outlander. I am not permitted by the fire with the families, so I am put at this end. The north door is about ten paces west of me and another about five paces to the east-south-east. The cooking pot is perhaps ten paces south-east. Take it if you want it, though I would not say I am welcome to it.

Here a debt is paid in work, outlander. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour that are counted in nushmeekos. When the months are worked the matter is over, so they say. Once, foreigners without a licence were kept to the docks at Lilmoth and barred from the city.

I am Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer. For now I am a guest of this marsh, though the hospitality has terms. I came to trade. I lost a cargo and was assessed months of labour. I cannot see when they will end, outlander.
There is a child called Little-Gecko, sitting some fifteen paces south-west of here. She is kind to me, which is more than I can say for most under this roof. I would thank you not to trouble her.
